observation_summary: The compiler failed to issue warnings for useless code (code without side effects) when that code was part of a comma-separated expression, specifically when it was not the rightmost element.
hypothesis: The logic in CheckSideEffects was incorrectly filtering out non-rightmost elements of comma expressions from side-effect analysis, preventing the detection of useless code in those positions.
prediction: The fix would involve removing the restrictive logic that only checked the rightmost element of a comma expression and instead applying the side-effect check to all elements of the comma expression.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows the removal of a complex conditional block that specifically handled Token.COMMA by checking if the node was the last child, and replacing it with a more general check that evaluates side effects for all nodes where the result is not used.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the procedural logic used to identify side effects within expressions. The original implementation had an incorrect algorithmic strategy that explicitly excluded non-rightmost elements of comma expressions from being flagged as useless. The fix replaces this flawed procedural logic with a more robust check that correctly identifies useless code regardless of its position in a comma sequence, which is a classic Algorithm/Method correction.
evidence_used: The bug report states that only the first element of a comma sequence was checked for side effects.
The fix diff removes the specific logic that checked if a node was the last child of a COMMA token.
The fix diff simplifies the condition to check for side effects whenever the result is not used, regardless of the parent type.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing a conditional, the root cause is the overall strategy for traversing and validating expressions, which is procedural (algorithmic) rather than just a missing guard.
